clue.text: Passed oral — it involved some English literature

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up and convoluted, so the preceding letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: A student recalls scraping through a viva on a set text from the English syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash hides the fact that 'it' belongs with the letters before it, not with 'involved'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic poem about the fall of Adam and Eve is a cornerstone work of the English canon.

clue.text: Love potion you need to strain, they say

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the word for strain is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to strain a liquid is to pass it through a filter

explanation.surface: Instructions for brewing a magic potion: pour it through a sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A philtre is a magic drink meant to make the drinker fall in love with someone.

clue.text: It turns up — and down

blocks.note: surface reading: something that keeps rising and falling, like a yo-yo
setter's reading: a spinning machine part whose name reads the same upward and downward, as a down entry is read both ways

explanation.surface: Something that keeps going up and down, like a yo-yo or a fairground ride.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'up' and 'down' are the two directions of reading, and this word survives both unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the revolving part of a motor, turbine or helicopter, so it is a thing that turns.

clue.text: Rate 11

blocks.note: first meaning: to rate someone, in an old sense, is to scold them severely
second meaning: the answer to 11 across, a word for beating someone

explanation.walkthrough: Rate here is not price or speed but the old verb meaning to berate.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone down is both to give them a sharp telling-off and, in older use, to give them a beating.

clue.text: Change hands over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word for hands is read backwards

blocks.note: paws are hands in a jokey sense, an animal's hands

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch the hand holding something.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, which is a kind of change.

clue.text: Fishes the lake and slips

definitions.note: plural noun for a collective noun

blocks.note: ling are long-bodied sea fish, and the plural is the same
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: An angler works the lake and loses footing on the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Slips are petticoats, women's underclothes, and underwear of that kind is collectively called lingerie.

clue.text: Brace of peacock

blocks.note: first meaning: a bar that supports a framework
second meaning: as a verb, to peacock is to parade about showing off

explanation.walkthrough: Brace looks like a pair of birds, as in a brace of pheasants; it is the structural support, and peacock is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A strut is a supporting rod in a structure, and to strut is to walk in a proud, showy manner.

clue.text: Girl given sixpence once, a tip as share of the profits

blocks.note: Di, short for Diana
six is VI in Roman numerals, and d was the symbol for a penny before British decimal currency in 1971
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: A girl is handed an old sixpence as a tip and treats it as her cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sixpence' splits into two pieces: the number six and the pre-1971 abbreviation for a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A dividend is the sum a company pays out to each shareholder from its earnings.

clue.text: A man in the dark, so to speak

indicators.note: speaking means saying it out loud, so the word for the dark counts by its sound

blocks.note: the dark hours after sunset

explanation.surface: A shadowy figure lurking unseen after nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the chess sense: each piece on the board is a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight is one of the chessmen, the piece that moves in an L shape.

clue.text: Generally you can find water here

blocks.note: first meaning: on the whole, for the most part
second meaning: inside a water main, or out ..., an old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally' reads like an adverb modifying the rest, but it stands alone as the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means mostly as an idiom, and literally describes a location inside a supply pipe or the ocean.

clue.text: Obtain control, we are told

definitions.note: obtain in its intransitive sense of prevail

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the word for control counts by its sound

blocks.note: a rein controls a horse, and to keep a tight rein is to keep control

explanation.surface: Reports say someone has seized power.
explanation.walkthrough: Obtain looks like get, but it has a formal sense, prevail or be in force, as in 'the rules that obtain here'.
explanation.definitionFit: When a state of affairs prevails it reigns, as in 'silence reigned', which is the formal sense of obtain.

clue.text: Most of the spots are cane

indicators.note: most but not all means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the word with its last letter cut
a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A teenager's acne problem treated with a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To cane someone is to beat them with a stick, and to thrash is to beat soundly.

clue.text: Furious? Learn to object

blocks.note: to see is to find out or understand
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: Advice to someone angry: learn to complain properly.
explanation.walkthrough: Object looks like the verb to protest; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone seething is boiling with rage, so the participle works as an adjective for intense anger.

clue.text: Use every means possible — lean on your leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the ones out in front, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter
opening letter

explanation.surface: Advice to pull every string you can and rely on your bosses.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is to put it to work, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Good-humoured -countryman accepts money

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the countryman wraps around the money

blocks.note: a peasant is a rural farm worker
L, for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A cheerful farmhand happily takes a payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant person is friendly and agreeable, in a good mood with others.

clue.text: Girl fell in with the wrong characters

blocks.note: a miss is a young woman
fell is an old word for an animal's hide, as is pelt

explanation.surface: A young woman got mixed up with a bad crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Fell looks like the past of fall, but it is the noun meaning skin or hide; characters are letters, not people.
explanation.definitionFit: A misspelt word is written with incorrect letters, and characters means letters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Untidy person in charge — county in the past upset about it

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, which in a down light reverses the order
the reversed county goes round it, meaning the charge already mentioned

blocks.note: the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county merged away in 1974 and so in the past when this was set
a child in your charge is in your care

explanation.surface: A scruffy official is upset about a county from times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcestershire was abolished in 1974 (it returned in 1998), which explains 'in the past'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarecrow is a ragged figure set in fields, and by extension any shabbily dressed, dishevelled person.

clue.text: A city girl

blocks.note: first meaning: the Tuscan capital, home of the Renaissance
second meaning: a woman's given name, as in Nightingale

explanation.walkthrough: 'A city girl' reads as one urban young woman; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence is the English name of Firenze in Italy and also a female first name.

clue.text: Pest flourished - dissipated energy catching it

indicators.note: something dissipated is scattered, so the letters are dispersed into a new order
to catch it is to hold it inside, referring back to the first piece of wordplay

blocks.note: taken as written
fl. stands for floruit, Latin for flourished, used for the active period of a historical figure

explanation.surface: A pest thrived, but its burst of energy faded away.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenflies are aphids, small sap-sucking insects that gardeners treat as a plague on roses.

clue.text: Encircle the French included in 5

definitions.note: an item of the answer to 5 down

blocks.note: to gird is to surround or bind round
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a French belt around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is a word for women's underclothes, and this answer is one kind of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a tight-fitting elastic undergarment for the hips and waist, one item among women's underwear.

clue.text: Players take it to be criminal

blocks.note: a group of musicians
taken as written

explanation.surface: Actors assume a role and become a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber, especially one in a gang, so a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Sedition and subversion aren't so very different

indicators.note: making something very different means rearranging its letters thoroughly

blocks.note: the seven letters, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A pedant insists that two political crimes are not really so different.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is betrayal of one's country, and stirring rebellion and undermining the state are both forms of it.

clue.text: One or two girls in the garden

definitions.note: one girl's name, or two names run together
a plant found in the garden

blocks.note: first meaning: a single woman's first name, which also splits into a flower name and a saint's name
second meaning: an aromatic herb grown in garden beds

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a single female name that also splits into two names, and is a common garden herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is an aromatic evergreen herb grown in gardens, and it is also a woman's first name.

clue.text: Chap has to leave the fruit

blocks.note: a chap is a man
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: A man is told he must give up the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangoes are sweet tropical stone fruits with orange flesh.

clue.text: Part of the head church

blocks.note: first meaning: the flat side of the skull beside the eye
second meaning: a building for worship

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head church' sounds like a cathedral or chief church; the clue splits after 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple is the area at each side of the forehead, and a temple is a place of worship.

clue.text: There's a bad smell about the river Tyne, by the sound of it

definitions.text: Tyne, by the sound of it
definitions.note: the definition is a word pronounced like Tyne

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the smell wraps round the river

blocks.note: pong is British slang for a stink
R, the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Complaint that the River Tyne in north-east England stinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyne is not the river here; spoken aloud it is tine, a point on a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine is one spike of a fork or antler, which is the same thing as a prong.

clue.text: Some nasty eye trouble

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and into the next

explanation.surface: A description of an unpleasant eye complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the edge of an eyelid, an unpleasant eye ailment.

clue.text: Some sheets — fifty-nine, roughly

indicators.note: roughly means not precisely, so the number word is given in a loose arrangement

blocks.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: Counting bedclothes: about fifty-nine of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated number splits into two parts, one Roman and one written out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bed sheets and pillowcases are collectively called linen, whatever they are made of.

clue.text: Disreputable number heading towards foreign port (American)

blocks.note: no. is the abbreviation for number
to means towards
Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian seaport
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A shady character sails for a port abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means famous for something bad, well known for ill repute.

clue.text: From Dover we can go any way - the transport's here

indicators.note: taking letters in any way you like means they can be arranged in any order

blocks.note: the twelve letters of this phrase

explanation.surface: A traveller at the Channel port of Dover finds a ride that can take them anywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go any way' sounds like a travel route; 'go' belongs to the letters and 'any way' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas-topped wagon was the vehicle of pioneers crossing the American West, so a form of transport.
